subject: Observability handshake: on-prem forwarding proxy & SIEM evidence routing
messages:
From: Ciara O'Neill <ciara.oneill@bluebank.com>

Cc: BlueBank SecOps <secops@bluebank.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: On-prem evidence export: proxy pattern questions

Rishi —

Thanks again for yesterday's walkthrough. We ran the internal follow-up with SecOps and a couple of questions came up as we sketch the enforcement window for the on-prem forwarder:

- Authentication model: we want to avoid long-lived service credentials inside our enclave. Can the forwarder perform short-lived client cert rotation via our internal PKI, or do you recommend mTLS with a Redwood-managed CA?
- Evidence residency: during bursts, will the proxy buffer events on disk? If so, what disk-level encryption/compliance controls are supported?
- SIEM mapping: we need a clear mapping doc (index names, event types, and trace correlation fields) so our ingestion pipeline can route to Splunk and to the audit-archive tier.

We attached a short list of sample events and the draft network ACLs. Can you share an operational pattern for the proxy and the recommended failover behavior if the hosted receiver is unreachable?

Appreciate it — Ciara

Ciara O'Neill
Director, Security Engineering
BlueBank Financial
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Ciara O'Neill <ciara.oneill@bluebank.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Hiro Tanaka <hiro_tanaka@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: On-prem evidence export: proxy pattern questions

Ciara —

Thanks for the clear list, and for the samples. High level answers up front, followed by an operational pattern and a quick fallback proposal.

1) Auth model: we support both short-lived client certs issued by your PKI (preferred) and mTLS using Redwood-managed certs. If your PKI rotates via an internal CA signing flow, the forwarder can auto-reload the keypair on cert issuance — we recommend a cert ttl <= 24h for high-security deployments.

2) Buffering: the forwarder uses an encrypted circular buffer by default (on-disk AES-256 using your KMS/HSM). By policy you can set volatile-only (memory) or persistent (disk) modes. Disk buffering is encrypted and the keys never leave your KMS. Retention and wipe policies can be enforced during deprovisioning.

3) SIEM mapping: attached is our mapping template. Key fields to preserve for trace correlation: request_id, model_id, shard_id, trace_parent, timestamp_ns. We recommend exporting two streams: (a) operational telemetry (metrics/traces) to your OpenTelemetry collector, and (b) evidence logs (redacted tokens, metadata) to Splunk HTTP Event Collector (HEC) with a parallel archival stream to your S3-compatible audit bucket.

Fallback: if the hosted receiver is unreachable, the proxy will switch to backpressure mode after N retries (configurable). In backpressure, forwarding is paused and the buffer grows to a configurable cap; once cap is reached, oldest-compliant entries are dropped following your retention policy. We can also configure an alternate endpoint in another region (Redwood Dedicated) for automatic failover.

I'll loop in Kimberly and Hiro for the tracehook and network ACL details. Would you be available tomorrow 10:00am PT for a 30-min readout?

— Rishi

Rishi Malhotra
Sr. Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Hiro Tanaka <hiro_tanaka@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: On-prem evidence export: proxy pattern questions

Quick notes from the tracehook/networking side — we should provide the customer with a single-page checklist they can apply to their enclave engineers. Draft below; I can convert to a one-pager after we align.

Checklist draft (operational):
- TLS & auth: support client cert rotation (PKI) + CRL/OCSP checks. Recommend cert TTL <= 24h; client cert validation enforced on every connection.
- Network ACLs: outbound to Redwood egress IP-set over TLS 443 only; allow secondary endpoint (dedicated) on port 7443. No inbound access allowed to the forwarder from internet.
- Trace correlation: add two headers on forwarded payloads: X-Redwood-TraceParent and X-Redwood-Request-ID. These map to trace_parent and request_id in your SIEM mapping.
- Sampling: default adaptive sampling at 1% for high-volume inference flows; customers can pin prompt-sets to 100% for quality/regression evaluation.
- Disk encryption: verify KMS integration (customer-managed) and ephemeral key wrap for buffer writes.
- Audit: maintain a daily digest file (signed) of forwarded batch metadata and place in your audit archive.

Network specifics (for your engineers):
- Egress hostnames: forwarder.redwood-inference.com -> resolve to advertised egress IPs; firewall to allow FQDNs or IP-set.
- TLS ciphers: ECDHE_RSA with AESGCM, TLS1.3 required.

Marissa: can you confirm the exact HEC index names we recommend for Splunk? I recall we suggested redwood_evidence and redwood_ops with separate hot/warm/cold policies. Also, Hiro — please add the tracehook sample payload for their SIEM team.

Kimberly

Kimberly Park
Security & Compliance Lead, Redwood Inference
